hook: A short, gentle file about a patchwork teddy bear that sews replacement organs. The format is the familiar one, procedures then description then a test log, but the temperature shifts quietly as you go. Read it to the very last line; the small document at the end changes how everything above it reads.
whyItMatters: Nothing in this file is a threat; the bear only ever heals, and every recorded subject recovers fully. That makes it a clean example of how the clinical report voice can carry warmth as well as dread: the flat, procedural language makes the bear's care feel more sincere, not less.
thingsToNotice:
The test log escalates on purpose: smoker's lungs patched from two swatches, a crocheted heart that beats before it vanishes, then whole layers of new skin over a burn victim, each handled with more confidence. The fourth subject, an eighteen-year-old, has a brain hemorrhage, and the bear cannot make anything for it. It scrabbles at the materials in distress for a minute, produces a king-size chocolate bar to offer instead, and spends the rest of the test clinging to the subject's leg with saline running from its eyes.

The addendum explains the bear: it was found taped to a red get-well card in a crashed mail truck, named Kairos the Bear and addressed to Tommy from his Grammy, saying only time can mend every wound. A present meant for a grandchild who was hurt or sick is why it always picks the youngest patient, and the card's line quietly admits the limit the fourth test just showed.
